entities.summary: Uppingham School is a public school in Uppingham, Rutland, England, founded in 1584 by Robert Johnson, the Archdeacon of Leicester, who also established Oakham School. The headmaster, Richard Maloney, belongs to the Headmasters' and Headmistresses' Conference and the school to the Rugby Group of British independent schools. Edward Thring was the school's best-known headmaster. His curriculum changes were adopted in other English public schools. John Wolfenden, headmaster from 1934 to 1944, chaired the Wolfenden Committee, whose report recommending the decriminalisation of homosexuality appeared in 1957.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Uppingham School's curriculum changes under Edward Thring were adopted by other English public schools, influencing educational practices in Britain. The school's headmaster, John Wolfenden, chaired the Wolfenden Committee, whose report on decriminalizing homosexuality contributed to significant social change.
